about: Records BibleData wrote twice for one person, each folded into the record that keeps its address; the same for the two records it writes for one Hebrew word of the creation, earth and heaven, by the owner's ruling of 2026-09-24, each pair carrying its own source; and, under 'splits', a record it wrote once for two men, whose second man's verses move to his own record, and where the ruling lists the verses the first man keeps, his words there name him again. The pairs come from an audit that showed a model every same-name, same-kind pair of records under one Strong number with their descriptions and verse lists: 1,021 pairs, 83 judged one referent, 40 of them with high confidence, 39 medium and 4 low. Every pair was then read again against its verses; the ones under 'merges' hold up, and the ones under 'declined' do not, or rest on a question the text leaves open. A pair read less surely than the list's own confidence carries its own. The record more words already name keeps its address, so fewer annotations move; on a tie the lower-numbered one does. Everything the folded record held moves with it, and its address, name, description and BibleData id stay on as a merged record, so a link to it still arrives and what the dataset said is not lost.
source: Essenthos: BibleData's same-name records compared pair by pair by claude-opus-5 (prompt records-1, 2026-09-06), and each pair it held to be one person read again against its verses by claude-opus-5-5, the high pairs on 2026-09-23 and the medium and low ones on 2026-09-24

merges.why: Both records are the Lord's brother James: the brother named in Matthew 13:55 and Mark 6:3, the James Peter reports to in Acts 12:17, who speaks at the council in Acts 15:13 and receives Paul in Acts 21:18, whom Paul calls 'the Lord's brother' in Galatians 1:19 and a pillar in 2:9, to whom the risen Lord appeared in 1 Corinthians 15:7, and who writes James 1:1 and is named as Jude's brother in Jude 1:1. The second record holds only these verses, all of them also under the first. Folded on the owner's word of 2026-09-25 ('merge them if they are one'). Whether James son of Alphaeus and James the Less, whose verses the first record also holds, are this man the text does not settle; that stays with PRB-0718.
1 Chronicles 9:11 and Nehemiah 11:11 are one list of the priests who settled in Jerusalem, written twice: in both Ahitub is Meraioth's father and 'the ruler of the house of God'.

Numbers 25:15 makes Zur, Cozbi's father, a head of a chief house in Midian, and Numbers 31:8 names Zur among the five kings of Midian slain in the war that avenged Peor; the second record's own description already asks whether they are one.

'Meremoth the son of Urijah, the son of Koz' (Nehemiah 3:4, 21) is the priestly house of Hakkoz whose sons could not prove their descent (Ezra 2:61, Nehemiah 7:63), and the first record already holds both verses.

1 Chronicles 6:20-21 and 6:39-43 are one Gershonite line read down and then up: Zimmah, Joah or Ethan, Iddo or Adaiah, Zerah, Jeaterai or Ethni. The Zerah of both is one man; Iddo and Adaiah are two spellings of his father.
Exodus 6:24's Abiasaph son of Korah is Chronicles' Ebiasaph (1 Chronicles 6:23, 37; 9:19), the same Korahite under two spellings; the first record already carries 'Ebiasaph' as a name.
1 Chronicles 9:11 and Nehemiah 11:11 are one list written twice: Zadok son of Meraioth son of Ahitub.
1 Chronicles 9:7 and Nehemiah 11:7 are one list of the Benjamites who settled in Jerusalem, written twice: Sallu son of Meshullam in both.

Nehemiah 12:7 lists Sallu among the priests who came up with Zerubbabel, and Nehemiah 12:20 names the same house a generation later as Sallai: the lists of 12:1-7 and 12:12-21 run in the same order, house for house.
1 Chronicles 9:12 and Nehemiah 11:12 are one list written twice: Adaiah son of Jeroham, of the line of Pashhur and Malchijah.
1 Chronicles 2:49 closes Caleb's genealogy with 'and the daughter of Caleb was Achsa', the Achsah of Joshua 15:16-17 and Judges 1:12-13.

The Levite of understanding brought to Ezra at the river Ahava (Ezra 8:18, 24) is the Sherebiah who stands with Jeshua and Hashabiah among the chief Levites of the same years (Nehemiah 8:7; 9:4-5; 10:12; 12:24); the second record already holds Ezra 8:18 and 8:24.
1 Chronicles 9:11 and Nehemiah 11:11 are one list written twice: Hilkiah son of Meshullam son of Zadok.
1 Chronicles 7:15 says 'the name of the second was Zelophehad: and Zelophehad had daughters', the Manassite of Numbers 26:33 and 27:1.

Jeremiah 37:3 sends 'Jehucal the son of Shelemiah' to the prophet, and Jeremiah 38:1 names 'Jucal the son of Shelemiah' among the princes who hear him: one of Zedekiah's officers, the second spelling a shortening of the first.

Iezer son of Gilead (Numbers 26:30) is the clan Abiezer of Joshua 17:2 and Judges 6:34; 1 Chronicles 7:18 counts the same Abiezer among the Manassite families through Hammolecheth, and the first record already holds that verse and the name Abiezer.
1 Chronicles 9:15 and Nehemiah 11:17 are one list written twice: Mattaniah son of Micha of the line of Asaph, and both records already claim Nehemiah 12:8.
'The sons of Hassenaah' who built the fish gate (Nehemiah 3:3) are 'the children of Senaah' of the return (Ezra 2:35, Nehemiah 7:38): the same name with the article, under the same number.
Jeremiah 38:1's 'Pashur the son of Malchiah' is the Pashur son of Melchiah whom Zedekiah sends to Jeremiah in 21:1, a verse the first record already holds.

1 Chronicles 3:15 lists Shallum as Josiah's fourth son, and Jeremiah 22:11 calls 'Shallum the son of Josiah' the king who reigned in his father's place: Jehoahaz. The first record already carries the name Shallum.
Nehemiah 12:10-11 and 13:28 both name Joiada son of Eliashib the high priest, and the first record already holds 13:28.
1 Chronicles 9:10 and Nehemiah 11:10 are one list written twice: Jedaiah, Joiarib, Jachin. The first record's own description cites Nehemiah 11:10.
1 Chronicles 9:12 and Nehemiah 11:12 are one list written twice, both naming Adaiah son of Jeroham; Nehemiah gives the longer line between Jeroham and Pashhur.
Eliashib son of Joiakim in the high-priestly succession of Nehemiah 12:10 and 12:22 is Eliashib the high priest of Nehemiah 3:1 and 13:4, 28.
1 Chronicles 24:28 repeats 23:21-22: Eleazar son of Mahli, who died and had no sons.
The Asaph whose sons are the singers of the return (Ezra 2:41, Nehemiah 7:44) and from whom Zichri descends (1 Chronicles 9:15) is David's chief musician, Asaph son of Berechiah.

1 Chronicles 6:14-15 names Jehozadak son of Seraiah, carried away by Nebuchadnezzar, and Haggai 1:1 names Joshua son of Josedech the high priest: one man, whom the second record already holds at 1 Chronicles 6:14-15.
Nehemiah 12:10 and 12:26 both name Joiakim son of Jeshua the high priest; 12:26 adds 'the son of Jozadak'.
1 Chronicles 6:47 names Mahli son of Mushi son of Merari, and 23:23 and 24:30 the same son of Mushi.
1 Chronicles 9:7 and Nehemiah 11:7 are one list written twice, and in both Meshullam is Sallu's father.

Genesis 36:2 names Anah the daughter of Zibeon, and 36:20-24 name Zibeon among the Horite chiefs of Seir with his son Anah; the one letter between Hivite and Horite is the variant the text is usually read through.

2 Kings 25:18 and Jeremiah 52:24 name Zephaniah the second priest, taken at Jerusalem's fall; he is Zephaniah son of Maaseiah the priest of Jeremiah 21:1, 29:25 and 37:3, and the second record already holds both lists.
1 Chronicles 3:17 names Salathiel son of Jeconiah, and Ezra 3:2 and Haggai 1:1 name Shealtiel the father of Zerubbabel; Matthew 1:12 joins the two in one line.

2 Samuel 11:21 asks 'Who smote Abimelech the son of Jerubbesheth? did not a woman cast a piece of a millstone upon him from the wall?': Gideon's son of Judges 9:53, Jerubbesheth being Jerubbaal with Baal's name replaced.
Jeremiah 36:10-12 names 'Gemariah the son of Shaphan the scribe', and Elasah son of Shaphan (29:3) is his brother: the sons of Josiah's scribe, whose son Ahikam the first record already names.

1 Chronicles 3:19 names Zerubbabel among the grandsons of Jeconiah, father of Meshullam and Hananiah; he is the only Zerubbabel of the Old Testament, and the governor's record already holds the verse. Chronicles makes him the son of Pedaiah where Ezra 3:2 and Haggai 1:1 make him the son of Shealtiel, Pedaiah's brother, and both fathers stand on the one man, each at its verse.

The priests 'of the sons of Harim' of Ezra 10:21 descend, by the dataset's own kinship, from the Harim to whom the third lot fell (1 Chronicles 24:8), and the house of Harim whose sons came up with Zerubbabel (Ezra 2:39, Nehemiah 7:42) is the same ancestor: one priestly house named for one man, as the singers of the return are Asaph's.

'Malchijah the son of Harim' repairs the wall beside 'Hashub the son of Pahath-moab' (Nehemiah 3:11), each named by his lay house, and the record of the lay house of Harim (Ezra 2:32) already holds the verse and names its Malchijah; the second record is that one word written again.

Nehemiah 3:11's Malchijah son of Harim, who repaired the tower of the furnaces, is the Malchijah of the sons of Harim who put away his foreign wife thirteen years before (Ezra 10:31); the first record already holds the verse.

Ezra 10:15's 'Shabbethai the Levite' is the Levite who taught the law (Nehemiah 8:7) and had the oversight of the outward business of the house of God (Nehemiah 11:16): the name is borne by no one else, and the first record already holds Ezra 10:15.

Nehemiah 9:4-5 sets Jeshua first of the Levites on the stairs, beside Bani and Kadmiel, in the assembly that makes the sure covenant of 9:38, and the Levites who seal it are headed by 'Jeshua the son of Azaniah, Binnui of the sons of Henadad, Kadmiel' (10:9). One assembly, one Jeshua.

The second record is the Levite who sealed the covenant (Nehemiah 10:11) and holds no verse and no word of its own; the first holds the verse, and its Hashabiah stands beside Sherebiah there as in Ezra 8:19, 24 and Nehemiah 12:24.
1 Chronicles 6:20-21 and 6:39-43 are one Gershonite line read down and then up, the reading its Zerah is folded on; Jahath stands in both above Zimmah, and the first record already holds 6:43.
The same line of 1 Chronicles 6:20-21 and 6:39-43: Zimmah stands three generations above Zerah in both, father of Joah or Ethan; the two lists differ only over the generation between him and Jahath.

Exodus 6:24 names Korah's sons Assir, Elkanah and Abiasaph, and 1 Chronicles 6:22-23 names Assir, Elkanah and Ebiasaph after Korah; 6:37 makes Ebiasaph Korah's own son, so the three of Chronicles are the brothers of Exodus, as the fold of Abiasaph and Ebiasaph already reads them.

'Pedaiah the son of Parosh' (Nehemiah 3:25) is of the house of Parosh, and the first record already holds the verse; the chief of the people who seal at Nehemiah 10:14 run Parosh, Pahath-moab, Elam, Zatthu, Bani, the houses of Ezra 2:3-10 in their order.

Both records hold the house of Immer of the return (Ezra 2:37, Nehemiah 7:40) and its sons who put away foreign wives (Ezra 10:20), and both make its Hanani and Zebadiah their descendants; the Immer to whom the sixteenth lot fell (1 Chronicles 24:14) is the ancestor that house is named for.

The second record is the Anaiah who sealed at Nehemiah 10:22, whom the first already holds; the name stands nowhere else but Nehemiah 8:4, beside Ezra at the reading of the law, in the month the covenant was sealed.

Henadad is the Levite house of Ezra 3:9 and Nehemiah 3:24 and 10:9 and no one else; Bavvai son of Henadad (Nehemiah 3:18) builds among 'their brethren' after the Levites of 3:17, and the first record already holds the verse.

Nehemiah 11:11 and 1 Chronicles 9:11 are one list written twice, and it is the high-priestly line of 1 Chronicles 6:12-13: Zadok, then Shallum or Meshullam, then Hilkiah and Azariah. The first record already holds both verses, and the second has no word of its own.

The second record is the Meshullam who stood against the putting away of the foreign wives (Ezra 10:15), whom the first already holds beside the chief man Ezra sent to Iddo the year before (Ezra 8:16).

1 Chronicles 9:11 and Nehemiah 11:11 are one list written twice, the list the folds of Ahitub, Meraioth and Hilkiah rest on: Zadok son of Meraioth in both, and both records hold both verses. Nehemiah 13:13's Zadok the scribe is another man, and his verse goes to a record of his own before the fold.

declined.why: Whether the Eliashib into whose son's chamber Ezra went (Ezra 10:6) is the high priest of Nehemiah's day is the old question of which of Ezra and Nehemiah came first; the text does not settle it.
The same question as the pair above, from the other record.

Luke 3:27 runs David's line through Nathan and Neri, not through Jeconiah; whether its Zorobabel son of Salathiel is the governor is argued both ways, and Luke's Shealtiel is kept apart for the same reason.
1 Chronicles 9:8 names two men: 'Ibneiah the son of Jeroham' and, at the end of Meshullam's line in the same verse, 'Ibnijah'. Two words, two men.
Nothing but the name and the generation joins the ruler of half Keilah (Nehemiah 3:17) to the Merarite who came with Ezra (Ezra 8:19).

The Kadmiel of the return under Zerubbabel (Ezra 2:40; 3:9) and the Kadmiel who stands on the stairs and seals the covenant under Nehemiah (9:4-5; 10:9) are ninety years apart; one may be the house the other founded, which is not one man.
Luke 3:27, as for the pair of the governor's records: whether Luke's Zorobabel son of Salathiel is the governor is argued both ways.

1 Chronicles 6 writes 'Amariah begat Ahitub, and Ahitub begat Zadok' twice, at 6:7-8 and at 6:11-12, six generations apart. The first Ahitub is the grandfather of David's Zadok's son Ahimaaz; the second is Ezra's ancestor (Ezra 7:2). Reading the second as the first written again is a conjecture about the text, not what it says.
The second record is folded into the second of the pair above, as one list written twice, and that pair's answer holds.

Both verses are already held by a third record, the Levite son of Jeshua of Ezra 8:33, whom the audit that joined these two kept apart from each of them. Whether the Jozabads of Ezra 8:33 and 10:23 and Nehemiah 8:7 and 11:16 are one Levite or more is a question of three records, and a fold of two does not answer it.

The Levite house of Jeshua and Kadmiel came up with Zerubbabel (Ezra 2:40, 3:9); the Jeshua who stands with Kadmiel on the stairs (Nehemiah 9:4-5) is ninety years later. The two names together are one house, not one man, as with Kadmiel himself.
Ninety years again, and Nehemiah 10:9 names this Jeshua's father, Azaniah, where the other is the head of a house of the return.

The two share the high-priestly verses (1 Chronicles 6:13, 9:11, Ezra 7:1, Nehemiah 11:11), but the second also holds the Hilkiah who stood by Ezra (Nehemiah 8:4), a priest of the return (Nehemiah 12:7, 21) and Gemariah's father (Jeremiah 29:3), and the person register reads it as the man of Nehemiah 8:4. A fold would put all of them on Josiah's high priest; the high-priestly verses have to leave it instead.
The second record is folded into the second of the pair above, and that pair's answer holds.

The Jedaiah whose sons returned is 'of the house of Jeshua' (Ezra 2:36), which does not fit the head of the second course (1 Chronicles 24:7), and the record also holds the priest who came up with Zerubbabel (Nehemiah 12:6). The text does not make a house that bears a course's name the house of that course's head.

1 Chronicles 9:10 names priests who lived in Jerusalem after the return, which Nehemiah 11:10 writes as 'Jedaiah the son of Joiarib'; the head of the first course (1 Chronicles 24:7) is five centuries earlier. One may be the house the other founded, which is not one man.

Nothing but the name and the generation joins the first of the priests who seal (Nehemiah 10:2) to the ruler of the house of God (Nehemiah 11:11); Seraiah is also the first house of the priestly lists of 12:1 and 12:12.
With the second record folded as above, this is the pair already declined: nothing but the name and the generation joins the ruler of half Keilah (Nehemiah 3:17) to the Merarite who came with Ezra.

The first record rests on Ezra 10:6, 'Johanan the son of Eliashib', and whether that Eliashib is the high priest is the question declined for Eliashib himself; the second already holds the Johanan of the high-priestly line at Nehemiah 12:22.

The first record is the house of Miniamin under which Joiakim's generation is counted (Nehemiah 12:17), the Miamin who came up with Zerubbabel (12:5); the priest with a trumpet at the dedication of the wall (12:41) is a man of Nehemiah's day who bears the house's name. A house and a man, as with Kadmiel.

1 Kings 4:5 writes 'the son of Nathan' twice, once for Azariah over the officers and once for Zabud the priest, and does not say they are brothers. If they are, their father is most likely the prophet or David's son, a third record, which this pair would not reach.

The verse the audit found on both (1 Chronicles 26:14) has since been moved to the first; the second is the Levite musician of the second degree (1 Chronicles 15:18-24, 16:5), and the person register keeps them apart. Name, era and office only.
One seals among the priests (Nehemiah 10:5), the other keeps the gates among the porters (Nehemiah 12:25); a priest is not a gatekeeper.

Nothing but the name, the generation and the office joins the Levite who put away his foreign wife (Ezra 10:23) to the Levite who called Israel to bless the Lord (Nehemiah 9:5); no one beside either is named in both.
Luke's Shealtiel, son of Neri (Luke 3:27), is kept apart for the reason Luke's Zerubbabel is.
The first record is folded into the first of the pair above, and that pair's answer holds.

The verse the audit read on both (Jeremiah 37:3) has since been moved to the second, so Jehucal's father at 37:3 and Jucal's at 38:1 is one record already. The son of Abdeel sent to seize Baruch (36:26) is joined to him by nothing but the name and the generation.

1 Chronicles 7:14 sets Ashriel, whom Manasseh's wife bore, against Machir, whom his concubine bore, which makes him the brother of Gilead's father where Numbers 26:31 makes Asriel Gilead's son. The clan may be one; the verses make two generations of it.

1 Chronicles 6 writes Ahitub begetting Zadok twice, at 6:8 and at 6:12. The verses that joined them for the audit (1 Chronicles 15:11, 16:39 and Ezekiel's sons of Zadok) have since been moved to David's Zadok, and what remains of the second is Ezra's ancestor.

The verses that joined them for the audit, Daniel 5:31 and chapter 6, have since been moved to the second: the first is the Persian of Ezra, Haggai and Zechariah, the second the Mede, son of Ahasuerus (Daniel 9:1).

Both hold Pashhur's father at Jeremiah 21:1 and 38:1, but the first is also the king's son whose dungeon held Jeremiah (38:6), and the second also the Malchijahs of Nehemiah 8:4, 10:3 and 12:42; the person register reads the first as the king's son. A fold would join all of them; the two verses have to leave the first instead.
Ezekiel 8:11 does not call Jaazaniah's father the scribe, and the scribe's sons the text names are Ahikam, Elasah and Gemariah. Name and generation only.
The first record is folded into the scribe's; the pair above answers it.

splits.why: Judges 4 and 5 are the prophetess who judged Israel, the wife of Lapidoth, who went up with Barak against Sisera and sang after the battle. The record of Rebekah's nurse (Genesis 35:8) held these verses because the dataset numbers the judge by the word for a bee, so the name resolved to the nurse's record alone, and the word the verses share was then read off them in every text as hers.

splits.name: Nathanael
splits.why: The project owner ruled on 2026-09-24 that the man John 1:45-49 and 21:2 name is Nathanael, as the text names him, and that his identification with Bartholomew, which BibleData follows by holding the name on its record of Bartholomew, is a later tradition and not the text's.

2 Samuel 13 is the story of Tamar the sister of Absalom, David's daughter (13:1), and 1 Chronicles 3:9 names her as the sister of David's sons. The record of Tamar the wife of Er (Genesis 38) held these verses because a reading of the Strong number chose the first record of the name.
2 Samuel 14:27 names the daughter born to Absalom, 'whose name was Tamar: she was a woman of a fair countenance' — Absalom's daughter, not Judah's daughter-in-law.

2 Kings 3 is the campaign of Jehoram son of Ahab, king of Israel (3:1), against Moab: he sends to Jehoshaphat (3:7), goes with the kings of Judah and Edom (3:9), and Elisha answers him only for Jehoshaphat's sake (3:14). The son of Jehoshaphat is not in the chapter.

Herod killed James the brother of John with the sword in Acts 12:2, so the James to whom Peter sends word in 12:17, who speaks at the council (15:13) and receives Paul (21:18), is another man. Galatians 1:19 names him 'James the Lord's brother', and 2:9 and 2:12 speak of the same James at Jerusalem.

Acts 8:1 says all were scattered 'except the apostles', and 8:14 that the apostles at Jerusalem sent Peter and John to Samaria when they heard what had been done there. The Philip who preached in Samaria and baptised the Ethiopian is Philip of the seven (6:5), whom 21:8 calls the evangelist, not the apostle.
John 14:22 is 'Judas saith unto him, not Iscariot', and Acts 1:13 lists Judas of James among the eleven after the betrayer's death. Neither verse is about Judas Iscariot.
Acts 1:13 prints 'Judas of James', as Luke 6:16 does; Thaddaeus is the name Matthew and Mark give in his place, and the verse does not print it.

Daniel 9:1 names Darius 'the son of Ahasuerus, of the seed of the Medes'. The king of Esther and of Ezra 4:6 reigns after Cyrus; the father of the Mede who took the kingdom at Babylon's fall is another man.

splits.name: Anah
splits.why: Genesis 36:2, 14 and 18 name Aholibamah the daughter of Anah, 36:24-25 name Anah the son of Zibeon and his children, and 1 Chronicles 1:40-41 repeat them. Beeri the Hittite of Genesis 26:34 is the father of another wife of Esau; that the two men are one is a harmonisation the text does not make, so Beeri keeps his verse and Anah's move to his own record.
The fold of Mattaniah son of Micha brought 2 Chronicles 20:14 with it, and that verse's Mattaniah is Jahaziel's ancestor in Jehoshaphat's day, not the man of the lists of Nehemiah.

2 Chronicles 28:9 is the prophet Oded at Samaria in the days of Ahaz and Pekah (28:1, 28:6). The record's own man is the father of Azariah, who prophesied to Asa in his fifteenth year (15:1, 15:10), more than a century and a half of the text's reigns earlier.
2 Chronicles 26:5 is the Zechariah 'who had understanding in the visions of God' in the days of Uzziah, two centuries before the prophet whose word came in the second year of Darius (ZEC 1:1).
Nehemiah 8:4 names a Zechariah standing at Ezra's left hand when he read the law, in Nehemiah's day; the verse does not make him the prophet of Darius' second year.

Nehemiah 12:16 names the head of the house of Iddo in the days of Joiakim (12:12). Whether he is the prophet the verse does not say, so he keeps his own record with the prophet as the open alternative.

Matthew 23:35 and Luke 11:51 name the Zacharias slain between the temple and the altar. His father's name is the prophet's father's and his death is that of Zechariah son of Jehoiada (2 Chronicles 24:20-21); the text does not say which he is, so he has a record of his own naming both.
Matthew 23:35 names Barachias as the father of the Zacharias slain between the temple and the altar; whether he is the prophet's father Berechiah is as open as whether his son is the prophet.

These verses name Mary Magdalene beside 'Mary the mother of James and Joses', 'the other Mary'. The record of Jesus' mother held her; the verses do not say she is his mother, and the encyclopedia holds a record of her.

Revelation names its writer as John, the servant of Jesus Christ in Patmos (1:1, 1:9), and does not say which John he is; tradition takes him for the son of Zebedee, and he keeps that as the open alternative.

1 Chronicles 2:18-49 is Caleb 'the son of Hezron' (2:18), 'the brother of Jerahmeel' (2:42), the Chelubai of 2:9, with his wives Azubah and Jerioth and his concubine Maachah. The relationships read from these verses were written onto the record of Caleb the son of Jephunneh.

1 Samuel 14:3 is 'Ahiah, the son of Ahitub, Ichabod's brother, the son of Phinehas ... the LORD's priest in Shiloh, wearing an ephod', with Saul at Gibeah, and 14:18 is Saul's word to him to bring the ark. The prophet Ahijah the Shilonite of 1 Kings 11-14 speaks to Jeroboam two generations later.

1 Chronicles 12:18 is 'Amasai, who was chief of the captains', on whom the spirit came when he pledged himself to David at Ziklag; the verse prints Amasai, not Amasa the son of Ithra whom Absalom set over the army.

Nehemiah 12:22 dates the record of the Levites 'to the reign of Darius the Persian', after the high priest Jaddua; the Darius of Ezra 4-6, Haggai and Zechariah is the king in whose second year the temple was rebuilt, generations earlier.

1 Kings 11:14 is 'the LORD stirred up an adversary unto Solomon, Hadad the Edomite: he was of the king's seed in Edom'. Hadadezer king of Zobah is the adversary of 11:23, whose servant Rezon fled from him.

Jeremiah 1:1 names 'Jeremiah the son of Hilkiah, of the priests that were in Anathoth'. Josiah's high priest served in the temple at Jerusalem (2 Kings 22:4), and the verse does not make Jeremiah's father the high priest.

1 Chronicles 6:13 'Shallum begat Hilkiah, and Hilkiah begat Azariah' is the high-priestly line, and 1 Chronicles 9:11, Ezra 7:1 and Nehemiah 11:11 trace Azariah and Ezra back through the same Hilkiah: the high priest of Josiah's day.
Nehemiah 8:4 names a Hilkiah among the men who stood at Ezra's right hand when he read the law, a century and a half after the high priest of that name.
Jeremiah 29:3 names 'Gemariah the son of Hilkiah', whom Zedekiah sent to Nebuchadnezzar with Elasah; the verse does not make his father the high priest or the priest of Zerubbabel's day.

The lists of the twelve name 'James the son of Alphaeus' (MAT 10:3, MRK 3:18, LUK 6:15); the Lord's brother is named with his brothers in Matthew 13:55 and Mark 6:3, and the verses do not make him one of the twelve.
Luke 6:16 is 'Judas the brother of James', in the Greek 'Judas of James': the James of that verse is named only as Judas's kinsman, and the encyclopedia holds him apart.
2 Samuel 13:5 is the counsel of 'Jonadab, the son of Shimeah David's brother' (13:3) to Amnon. Jehonadab the son of Rechab of 2 Kings 10 and Jeremiah 35 lived in Jehu's day.
Acts 18:7 names 'a certain man's house, named Justus', Titius Justus in the critical editions, at Corinth; Titus is Paul's companion of Galatians 2 and 2 Corinthians and is not in the verse.
Luke 3:29 is 'Jose, which was the son of Eliezer' in Luke's genealogy, printed Ἰησοῦ in the critical editions; the brother of Jesus is not in the verse.
Acts 4:36 is 'Joses, who by the apostles was surnamed Barnabas, a Levite, and of the country of Cyprus'; the brother of Jesus is not in the verse.

The priest Pashhur son of Malchijah of 1 Chronicles 9:12 and Nehemiah 11:12, the house of priests named after him (Ezra 2:38, 10:22, Nehemiah 7:41) and the Pashhur who sealed the covenant among the priests (Nehemiah 10:3); the record keeps Zedekiah's envoy of Jeremiah 21:1 and 38:1, whom the text does not make that priest.
Jeremiah 21:1 names Pashur the son of Melchiah, Zedekiah's envoy; Gedaliah's father of Jeremiah 38:1 is not in the verse.
1 Chronicles 9:12 and Nehemiah 11:12 name Malchijah as the father of the priest Pashhur, generations before the Malchiah who stood at Ezra's left hand (Nehemiah 8:4).
Nehemiah 10:3 is a priest who sealed the covenant and 12:42 a Malchijah at the dedication of the wall; the text does not make either of them the man at Ezra's left hand.
Jeremiah 38:1 names Pashur the son of Malchiah among Zedekiah's princes, and 38:6 that Malchiah's dungeon; the priest of Ezra's day is not in the verse.
Acts 19:22 is the Erastus whom Paul sent into Macedonia with Timothy, held as erastus; the verse does not call him the city's chamberlain.
Joshua 10:28 and 12:16 name the king of Makkedah; Horam king of Gezer is not in them.
1 Chronicles 6:9 is 'Ahimaaz begat Azariah, and Azariah begat Johanan', the grandfather of the Azariah of 6:10.
2 Chronicles 26:17-20 is Azariah the priest who withstood King Uzziah, held as azariah-20, and the verses do not place him in the line of 1 Chronicles 6.
Nehemiah 10:2 is a priest who sealed the covenant under Nehemiah, three centuries after Hezekiah's chief priest of 2 Chronicles 31:10.
Nehemiah 8:7 is a Levite who helped the people understand the law; the verse does not make him Azariah the son of Maaseiah, who repaired the wall beside his house (Nehemiah 3:23).
1 Chronicles 27:32 is 'Jonathan David's uncle ... a counsellor, a wise man, and a scribe', held as jonathan-15; the son of Shimea is David's nephew.
Jeremiah 35:4 is Maaseiah the son of Shallum, the keeper of the door in Jehoiakim's day, centuries after the Levite with the psaltery of 1 Chronicles 15:18-20.
Nehemiah 8:7 is a Levite who helped the people understand the law; the verse does not make him the Maaseiah at Ezra's right hand (8:4).
Nehemiah 10:25 is a chief of the people who sealed the covenant; the verse does not make him the Maaseiah at Ezra's right hand.
Nehemiah 12:42 is a Maaseiah at the dedication of the wall; the verse does not make him the Maaseiah at Ezra's right hand.
Nehemiah 10:10 is a Levite Shebaniah who sealed the covenant, held as shebaniah-4; the text does not make him the Shebaniah of 9:4-5.
Ezra 2:2 and Nehemiah 7:7 are the Nehemiah who came up with Zerubbabel, about ninety years before the governor son of Hachaliah.
2 Chronicles 35:9 is a chief of the Levites at Josiah's passover, about ninety years after Hezekiah's Cononiah.

1 Chronicles 23:8, 26:21-22 and 29:8 are Jehiel the son of Laadan the Gershonite, over the treasures of the house of the LORD; the Levite with the psaltery of 15:18-20 is not called his son or a Gershonite.
2 Chronicles 35:8 is Jehiel a ruler of the house of God at Josiah's passover, held apart from the son of Heman of Hezekiah's day.

1 Samuel 12:9 recalls the king of Moab into whose hand the LORD sold Israel in the days of the judges, which is Eglon (Judges 3:12-14), not the former king of Moab from whom Sihon took the land (Numbers 21:26).
1 Chronicles 15:24 and 16:6 are Benaiah among the priests with trumpets; the Benaiah of 15:18-20 and 16:5 is a Levite of the second degree with a psaltery.
1 Chronicles 16:6 is Jahaziel among the priests with trumpets; Jaaziel of 15:18 is a Levite of the second degree.
2 Chronicles 35:9 is a chief of the Levites at Josiah's passover, about ninety years after the Jeiel of 29:13.
2 Chronicles 35:9 is a chief of the Levites at Josiah's passover, held as shemaiah-23, about ninety years after the Shemaiah of 31:15.
Nehemiah 8:7 is a Levite who helped the people understand the law, held as akkub-5; the porter Akkub is not in the verse.
1 Chronicles 15:24 is Amasai among the priests with trumpets, held as amasai-2; the son of Elkanah of 6:25 and 6:35 is a forefather of Samuel.
2 Chronicles 29:12 is Mahath the son of Amasai in Hezekiah's day, held as amasai-3.
Nehemiah 8:7 is a Levite who helped the people understand the law, held as hanan-6; the house of temple servants of Ezra 2:46 is named after another Hanan.
Nehemiah 10:26 is a chief of the people who sealed the covenant, held as hanan-9; the Levite of 8:7 is not in the verse.
1 Chronicles 15:24 is Zechariah among the priests with trumpets; the Zechariah of 15:18-20 is a Levite of the second degree with a psaltery.
Ezra 10:23 is a Levite who had taken a foreign wife, held as jozabad-7.
Nehemiah 8:7 is a Levite who helped the people understand the law, held as jozabad-8.
2 Chronicles 17:7 is a prince Jehoshaphat sent to teach in the cities of Judah, held as obadiah-the-teaching-prince; the son of Shemaiah of 1 Chronicles 9:16 lived after the return.
2 Chronicles 35:8 is Zechariah a ruler of the house of God at Josiah's passover, held as zechariah-26; the overseer of the repairs of 34:12 is not named a ruler.
2 Chronicles 19:11 is Jehoshaphat's chief priest, whom the verse does not place in a line; held apart until the text says he is the son of Azariah of 1 Chronicles 6:11.
Nehemiah 10:20 is a chief of the people who sealed the covenant, held as meshullam-the-covenant-chief.
Nehemiah 10:7 is a priest who sealed the covenant, held as meshullam-17.
Nehemiah 12:16 is the head of the house of Ginnethon in Joiakim's days, held as meshullam-18.
Nehemiah 12:36 is a musician at the dedication of the wall, held as hanani-5; Nehemiah's brother is not in the verse.
Hebrews 11:5 is Enoch who was translated that he should not see death, the son of Jared (Genesis 5:24), not Cain's son.
Hosea 1:3 is Gomer the daughter of Diblaim, Hosea's wife, held as gomer-2; the son of Japheth is not in the verse.
Nehemiah 13:13 is the Levite Pedaiah whom Nehemiah made a treasurer, held as pedaiah-7; the verse does not make him the man at Ezra's left hand (8:4).
2 Samuel 23:24 and 1 Chronicles 11:26 are Elhanan the son of Dodo of Bethlehem, one of the thirty; the giant-slayer is the son of Jaare-oregim (2 Samuel 21:19).
1 Chronicles 6:45 is Amaziah the son of Hilkiah in the line of Ethan the Merarite, generations before the priest of Bethel who stood against Amos (Amos 7:10-14).
Mark 2:14 and Luke 5:27-29 are Levi the son of Alphaeus, the publican; the verses do not make him James the son of Alphaeus.
1 Chronicles 6:36 is Joel the son of Azariah in the line of Heman, generations before Samuel's son.
Nehemiah 12:42 is an Ezer at the dedication of the wall, not the son of Hur of 1 Chronicles 4:4.
Nehemiah 12:42 is an Ezer at the dedication of the wall; the verse does not make him the Ezer son of Jeshua who repaired the wall (3:19).
1 Chronicles 12:9 is Ezer the first of the Gadites who came to David, held as ezer-4; the son of Hur is a man of Judah.
Jeremiah 29:21 is Maaseiah the father of the false prophet Zedekiah in the exile, held as maaseiah-19; the priest of Ezra 10:18 lived a century later.
Jeremiah 36:12 is Delaiah the son of Shemaiah among the princes, held as shemaiah-22; the verse does not call his father the Nehelamite.
Jeremiah 42:1 is Jezaniah the son of Hoshaiah; whether he is the Maachathite's son of 2 Kings 25:23 and Jeremiah 40:8 the text does not settle, so he is held as a man of his own who says so.
